ideas.description: Exploit: spend the margin on the epoch dial, with a branch that depends on I038, which is still running. Base: the current tip E023 (9.0 true epochs), or I038's recipe if I038 is kept. Branch (a): if I038 is kept with a held-out seeds 3–12 gain of at least 0.15 pp, cut 0.5 true epoch to 8.5 true epochs (212 steps at batch 2000). This is E020's step count plus I038's averaging. Branch (b): otherwise, cut 0.25 true epoch to 8.75 true epochs (219 steps). In both branches the resolution phases stay fixed fractions of total steps (40/30/30, so the 32 px tail keeps its 30% share), and the LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules stretch to the new step count, as in E008/E020/E023. Compiled shapes are unchanged and error_on_recompile stays on. The step count changes RNG use, so in the same session also run held-out seeds 3–12 (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Keep only if seeds 0–2 clear 0.753 and the held-out mean is at least 0.7535. Do not re-roll RNG streams to chase a lucky seeds 0–2 draw.
ideas.expected: Branch (b): time falls about 2.7% (about 0.17 s), from 6.20 to about 6.03 s. Held-out mean falls 0.05–0.2 pp (dial: 0.44 pp per epoch), from 0.7556 to about 0.7545. Seeds 0–2 land at 0.751–0.758, about a 70% chance of clearing 0.753. Branch (a): time about 5.86 s, held-out about 0.7533 plus I038's gain. A held-out drop of more than 0.25 pp per 0.25 epoch means the dial steepens below 9 epochs.

ideas.description: Explore/exploit: a FreezeOut-style backward truncation, a mechanism not yet tried in this loop. On the E023 tip, put group-1 conv filters (Muon) and the whitening bias plus group-1 BN params (SGD) in their own param groups. Their LR schedule follows the global triangle up to its peak, then decays linearly to 0 at 75% of total steps. The other groups keep their schedules. For the last 25% of steps, all of them at 32 px, detach group 1's output before group 2, and use a second compiled train step that does no group-1 or whitening backward and leaves group-1 params out of the Muon/SGD update. Group-1 BN still runs in train mode, and Lookahead still averages every param. Capture both 32 px step variants (full and truncated) in build with channels_last synthetic tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Back-of-envelope: group 1 is about 20% of conv MACs at the largest maps, so skipping its weight-grad and input-grad work saves about 14–18% of a 32 px step (including memory-bound BN/GELU backward), applied to about 2.0 s of tail time. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time falls 4–6% (about 0.25–0.35 s), to about 5.85–5.95 s. Held-out mean falls 0.05–0.3 pp from 0.7556. The deciding number is the exchange rate. Better than 1.5 s/pp (e.g. 0.3 s for 0.2 pp or less) beats the epoch dial and supports H2.6.1, and the next step tests freezing at 65%. If time falls under 3%, the backward through group 1 is not the cost the MAC model says it is (feed this into I040/H6). A loss above 0.35 pp means early layers keep learning usefully at the end of short CIFAR-100 runs.

ideas.description: Explore: proposes a new H2.4 child. Drop easy examples using free per-sample losses from the main net, with no proxy. The committee vetoed I041 for the proxy's cost; this version adds no extra forward passes. On the E023 tip, change the compiled train step to return the per-sample loss (reduction='none', then mean for backward) and scatter it into a GPU loss buffer indexed by sample id. The buffer is created and reset in prepare. From epoch 2 onward, each epoch's shuffled order uses only the 90% of samples with the highest loss in the previous pass (torch.topk on the GPU, then the usual GPU shuffle). The batch stays at 2000 and the ragged remainder is dropped. Total steps fall from 225 to about 205 (1 + 8×0.9 epoch-equivalents). The resolution phases (40/30/30), LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules are fractions of the new total step count. Alternating flip still uses each sample's own pass parity. Warm up the modified step in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time falls 8–10% (about 0.5–0.6 s), to about 5.6–5.7 s. A uniform cut of the same steps on the epoch dial would cost about 0.35 pp (held-out about 0.752). Selection is worth keeping if the held-out mean drops 0.2 pp or less (to 0.7536 or higher), so it beats the dial at better than 2.5 s/pp. A drop of 0.35 pp or more means easy examples still carry signal in 9-epoch CIFAR-100 runs (or that stale losses pick noisy or ambiguous images), which would refute this child.

ideas.description: Exploit, the time-favorable direction of H5 (the committee vetoed I026's smaller batch as clear harm). On the E023 tip at the same true epoch count (9.0), raise batch from 2000 to 2500, which gives exactly 20 steps per epoch, 180 steps instead of 225. Scale the SGD-group (BN, whitening bias, head) lr linearly with batch the way the code does now, and leave Muon lr at 0.24 and momentum at 0.6. Express the resolution, LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules as fractions of the new step count, keeping the 5-step Lookahead period. Recapture every resolution's graph at batch 2500 in build, with error_on_recompile on. Check peak memory at 32 px. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time falls 1–3% (fixed per-step overhead is about 5% of train time, plus better GPU use at 24 px), to about 6.0–6.15 s. Held-out mean moves −0.35 to +0.1 pp, median about −0.1. A loss of 0.1 pp or less with at least 1.5% time saved supports H5.1.1, Muon's large critical batch. A loss of 0.25 pp or more means step count matters even under Muon, which closes the batch lever.

ideas.description: Exploit, a time-neutral booster to fund trims. On the E023 tip, double only the Muon lr for conv filters from 0.24 to 0.48. The SGD groups, momentum 0.6, wd ×0.5, batch, schedules, epochs, resolution and Lookahead/EMA all stay the same. E014 (×1.5 at the old wd) moved +0.09 pp. The wd ×0.5 base and E006's large unexplained Muon gain leave the upper side of the lr range untested. If lr is baked into the graph as a constant, recapture the graphs. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2, since a single 3-seed difference under 0.4 pp is unreadable.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±1%). Held-out mean moves −0.25 to +0.3 pp from 0.7556, median about +0.05. A held-out gain of at least 0.2 pp supports H1.5.6 and funds about 0.5 epoch of trimming (pair it with the epoch-trim idea). A loss of at least 0.15 pp puts the optimum at 0.24–0.36 and ends the Muon lr grid.

drop.reason: E024's lesson applies here. 20 px gives off-grid feature maps (19/9/4/2) whose autotuned kernels tile poorly, so the modelled 3.5% pixel saving would likely shrink to about 2%, below the 4% bar. The committee has 0/4 improve votes and 3/4 harm votes, and members agree (conflict 0). Expected value is too low to justify a run.

All four members forecast harm and none an improvement. Global LS was flat between 0.2 and 0.3 (E013). The EfficientNetV2 size-dependent regularization effect relies on large regularization ranges, not LS 0.15 vs 0.3 in a 9-epoch run, so a 0.2 pp gain is unlikely and would not change time.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E023: 9.0 true epochs, 6.20 s, held-out mean 0.7556, about 0.26 pp above the bar. So far the epoch dial (about 1.5 s per pp) is the cheapest trade measured; resolution and width cuts traded at 0.5–1.0 s per pp.

**New ideas**
- **Epoch trim (priority 4):** it depends on I038. If I038 adds at least 0.15 pp on held-out seeds, cut to 8.5 epochs; otherwise cut to 8.75 epochs (about 6.03 s, held-out about 0.7545).
- **FreezeOut, H2.6.1 (priority 4):** stop backprop through group 1 and the whitening bias for the last 25% of steps. Their LR is annealed to 0 by that point. Expected time is down 4–6%, and it wins if it costs 0.2 pp or less.
- **Easy-example dropping without a proxy, new H2.4 child (priority 3):** reuse each sample's loss from the previous pass, which costs nothing extra, and skip the easiest 10% from epoch 2 on. Expected time is down 8–10%. It beats the epoch dial if the held-out mean drops 0.2 pp or less.
- **Batch 2500, H5.1.1 (priority 2):** the faster direction of the batch lever, after the committee vetoed the smaller batch in I026.
- **Muon lr 0.48, H1.5.6 (priority 2):** a booster that doesn't change time, judged on held-out seeds.

**Dropped**
- **I035:** 20 px gives odd feature-map sizes that tile poorly (the E024 lesson), so the time saving would likely fall below 4%. The committee forecast harm.
- **I039:** label smoothing has been flat (E013), and all four members forecast harm.

**Kept:** I040, the per-layer profiling diagnostic, at priority 2. Its "harm" votes don't mean much because it changes nothing in the recipe, and it decides H6/H2.2.4.

The queue now holds 6 queued ideas, with I038 still running.
